government.note: The President is directly elected for six years (two-round system, at most two consecutive terms) and conducts foreign policy together with the Government; the Prime Minister is elected by Parliament and leads the Government, which needs Parliament's confidence. The new Constitution of Finland took effect on 1 March 2000, the day Tarja Halonen took office, and reduced the President's powers in favour of the Prime Minister. On 1 January 2000 Martti Ahtisaari was President and the first round of the 2000 presidential election (16 January) had not yet been held.

title.en: President of the Republic of Finland

offices.note: The President takes office on the first day of the month after the election. The Prime Minister acts if the President is temporarily unable to serve; on a permanent vacancy a new election is held. There is no vice president.

system.note: Open-list PR by D'Hondt in multi-member electoral districts (15 in 1999 and 2003, 13 today) with no national threshold; Åland always elects one member. seats_2000 is the March 1999 result; the Åland seat (Liberals for Åland) is counted as others. Individual party switches before 1 January 2000 were not checked.
